en.name: Epazote
en.summary: Fresh epazote keeps 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Beyond that, freeze it: the leaves blacken but the flavour holds, and epazote is only ever used cooked.
en.pantry: Epazote should not be left at room temperature. It is a soft-stemmed, high-moisture herb that wilts quickly in a warm kitchen, and unlike basil it gains nothing from being kept out. If you have picked or bought a bunch, get it into the fridge the same day. A few hours in a glass of water while you cook is fine; a few days on the worktop is not.
en.fridge: 2–3 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Stand the stems in a little water like cut flowers, or wrap them in a barely damp cloth inside a bag. Epazote bruises black wherever it is crushed, so store the sprigs loose rather than packed tightly into a box, and do not put anything heavy on top of them. Do not wash it until you cook — wet leaves on a soft-stemmed herb collapse within a day or two. Remember that this figure is read across from coriander rather than measured for epazote.
en.freezer: Freezing turns epazote's leaves black and slack, but the flavour survives and epazote is only ever used cooked — a bag of frozen sprigs dropped into a pot of black beans works perfectly well. Do not expect to garnish with it.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Drop frozen sprigs straight into the pot; thawed epazote is limp and wet and will not hold up to handling.
spoilage: Blackened, slimy leaves, usually where the sprigs were crushed.
A sour or fermented smell instead of the herb's own pungent, petrol-like sharpness.
Slime at the cut ends or cloudy water in the glass.
Mould on the stems, especially in a tightly closed box.
tips: Store the sprigs loose; epazote bruises black where it is squashed.
Do not wash it until you are about to cook.
Use a sprig or two rather than a handful — it is a strong, assertive herb.
Freeze whole sprigs for beans and stews; the flavour survives even though the looks do not.

faq.q: How long does fresh epazote keep?
faq.a: 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. That figure is read across from fresh coriander; no agency publishes one for epazote.
Yes, though the leaves go black and slack. The flavour survives, and since epazote is always used cooked, frozen sprigs work well in beans and stews.

faq.q: Can epazote be kept at room temperature?
faq.a: No timeline is published for it. It is a soft, high-moisture herb that wilts quickly, so refrigerate it the day you get it.

zh.name: 土荊芥（epazote）
zh.summary: 新鮮土荊芥放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 2～3 週。再久就用冷凍：葉子會變黑，但風味留得住，而土荊芥本來就一律煮過才吃。
zh.pantry: 土荊芥不該放在室溫。它是莖軟、含水量高的香草，在溫暖的廚房裡很快就萎軟；而且和羅勒不同，它放在外面得不到任何好處。買來或摘來的一把，請當天就放進冰箱。煮菜時先插在水杯裡幾小時沒問題；在檯面上放好幾天就不行了。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 2～3 週。把莖插進一點水裡像插花，或用微濕的布包起來裝袋。土荊芥被壓到的地方會瘀黑，所以請讓枝條鬆散地放，不要硬塞進盒子，上面也別壓重物。要下鍋時才洗——軟莖香草的葉子一濕，一兩天內就會塌掉。也請記得，這個數字是比照香菜而來，不是針對土荊芥測出來的。
zh.freezer: 冷凍會讓土荊芥的葉子變黑變軟，但風味留得住；而土荊芥反正一律是煮過才吃的——一袋冷凍枝條丟進一鍋黑豆裡完全沒問題。只是別指望拿它擺盤。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。直接把冷凍枝條丟進鍋裡；解凍過的土荊芥又軟又濕，根本禁不起翻動。
spoilage: 葉子發黑、黏滑，通常出現在被壓到的地方。
聞起來酸或有發酵味，而不是它本身那股帶汽油感的衝味。
切口變黏滑，或杯子裡的水變混濁。
莖上長霉，密閉盒子裡尤其容易。
tips: 枝條鬆散放；土荊芥被壓到就會瘀黑。
一次用一兩枝就好——這是味道很強勢的香草。
整枝冷凍留給燉豆和燉菜；外觀沒了，味道還在。

faq.q: 新鮮土荊芥可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 週。這個數字是比照新鮮香菜而來，沒有機關公布土荊芥的期限。
可以，只是葉子會變黑變軟。風味留得住；既然它一律煮過才吃，冷凍枝條拿來燉豆、燉菜很好用。
它沒有公布常溫的期限。它是柔軟、含水量高的香草，很快就萎軟，所以拿到當天就該冷藏。
